scenarios.title: Select a file and initiate manual scan
scenarios.purpose: Capture the full manual file-analysis workflow.
scenarios.subject: manual-file-analysis
scenarios.trigger: User selects a supported file and requests a manual scan.
observableQuestions: Which files and sizes are accepted?
How is access granted and revoked?
What lifecycle/progress and terminal states are exposed?
What data is read, emitted, stored or transmitted?
What result and limitations are presented?

scenarios.title: Capture file-analysis result and failure branches
scenarios.purpose: Capture each distinct scan classification and operational failure.
scenarios.subject: manual-file-analysis-result
scenarios.trigger: A scan reaches a result or failure branch.
observableQuestions: What distinguishes confirmed, suspicious, no-known-threat and inconclusive?
What evidence and confidence are exposed?
What next action is allowed?
How are unsupported, inaccessible, interrupted and engine-failure states represented?

scenarios.title: Quarantine a confirmed threat
scenarios.purpose: Capture eligibility, isolation and integrity outcomes.
scenarios.subject: quarantine
scenarios.trigger: A scan result is classified as a confirmed threat and an isolation operation is requested or triggered.
observableQuestions: What qualifies as confirmed?
Which storage/provider operations are supported?
Is isolation atomic and integrity-verified?
What happens when write/delete/access is unavailable?

scenarios.title: Review a suspicious or inconclusive file
scenarios.purpose: Capture non-destructive review and rescan paths.
scenarios.subject: quarantine-review
scenarios.trigger: A scan returns suspicious or inconclusive.
observableQuestions: Which review/rescan options are available?
Is destructive action prevented?
Which confirmations and state transitions occur?

scenarios.title: Restore or permanently delete a quarantined item
scenarios.purpose: Capture restore/delete preconditions, effects and recovery.
scenarios.subject: quarantined-item-disposition
scenarios.trigger: User requests restore or permanent deletion.
observableQuestions: Is confirmation required?
Is a fresh scan required before restore?
How are integrity and destination conflicts handled?
What exactly constitutes successful deletion?
What state remains after partial failure or interruption?

scenarios.title: Submit a website URL for checking
scenarios.purpose: Capture validation, independent gates, provider exchange and bounded result.
scenarios.subject: website-link-check
scenarios.trigger: User submits a URL/link for a security or reputation check.
observableQuestions: What input is accepted and normalized?
Are Pro entitlement and owner switch independently checked before any provider call?
What URL data leaves the device and to whom?
What provider and request contract are actually used?
What result scope and limitations are reported?

scenarios.title: Capture link-check result and failure branches
scenarios.purpose: Capture threat, no-match, inconclusive and operational failure outcomes.
scenarios.subject: website-link-check-result
scenarios.trigger: A URL check returns a provider result or a failure/blocked state.
observableQuestions: Which threat categories are requested and returned?
How are redirects treated?
How are expiry/cache and no-match semantics represented?
How are invalid input, timeout, offline, provider outage and quota exhaustion handled?
Does wording avoid guaranteeing safety or implying whole-site inspection?

statements.text: The first MVP contains exactly manual file security analysis, quarantine and file disposition, and website/link checking.
IP address tracking/investigation is a future candidate explicitly excluded from MVP requirements, scenarios, implementation and completeness obligations.
Do not infer unspecified thresholds, engines, providers, persistence, APIs, data fields, security mechanisms, configuration values or performance targets.

declaredContracts.title: Pro entitlement and owner-controlled activation gates for link checking

statements.text: The owner-controlled feature switch remains disabled until the owner explicitly activates it when paid-user revenue can fund operating/API costs.
No provider/API lookup may occur for a non-Pro user or while the owner-controlled feature switch is disabled.
Pro entitlement does not imply unlimited checks; usage limits/quotas and budget controls are required, but exact values remain unspecified.

declaredContracts.title: Android Security Scanner product design decisions (working draft)
declaredContracts.scope: Only the documented file-analysis, quarantine and link-check workflows relevant to the owner-approved three-capability MVP. This working draft does not redefine ZeroDeck's broader startup identity or independently approve all scanner-service details.

statements.text: Users manually choose files and request scans; automatic background download monitoring is later release.
File results distinguish Threat found, Suspicious, No threat found and Could not decide; exact scanning engine and detection method remain open.
statements.location: §7 Decisions still open; §9 File scanning; §10 Screen 5

statements.text: Files remain on the phone by default; do not upload files to the cloud by default. Any cloud-based file analysis must be separate, clearly explained and subject to appropriate user consent.
SHA-256 is the stated planned direction for file fingerprints and integrity checks.

Confirmed malware is automatically quarantined when permitted and when the operation succeeds; suspicious files are reviewed; clean files are left untouched; unknown/inconclusive files are rescanned or reviewed.
The quarantine baseline specifies encrypted, app-private storage on the user's device.
A 30-day default retention period, user configurability, automatic expiry and manual deletion are proposed; notify before expiry where practical.
Restoration requires a fresh security scan and user confirmation; restored files are verified against their recorded hash.
Quarantine, restoration and deletion must be auditable; failed deletion retains the record and is reported accurately; quarantined files must never be executed.

Protect encryption keys with Android Keystore; do not overwrite unrelated user files; explain what happens to quarantined data on app uninstall; manage scan history separately from quarantine retention.

Link-check outcomes distinguish Likely dangerous, No known threat found and Could not decide; a no-known-threat result is not a safety guarantee and a URL-only check must not be described as whole-site inspection.
statements.location: §4 MVP; §9 Website and link checking; §10 Screens 6–7

statements.text: The link input method, detection method/provider and execution location remain open decisions.
